learningObjectives.title: Camera techniques (aperture, shutter speed, ISO, composition)

questions.q: In what units is a camera's aperture measured?
questions.explain: Aperture is expressed as f-stops or f-numbers, such as f/2.8 or f/16, which describe the size of the lens opening.

questions.q: What is the main effect of using a fast shutter speed?
options: It widens the depth of field
questions.explain: A fast shutter speed exposes the sensor briefly, freezing motion so moving subjects appear sharp.

questions.q: What does a small f-number such as f/2.8 produce?
options: A wide aperture and a shallow depth of field
A narrow aperture and a deep depth of field
questions.explain: A small f-number means a wide lens opening, letting in more light and giving a shallow depth of field with a blurred background.

questions.q: What does the ISO setting on a camera control?
options: The size of the lens opening
questions.explain: ISO measures how sensitive the sensor is to light; a higher ISO brightens the image in darker conditions.

questions.q: What is a common side effect of using a very high ISO setting?
options: Increased noise or grain in the image
Reduced sharpness at the edges only
questions.explain: Raising the ISO amplifies the signal and introduces visible noise or grain, reducing image quality.

questions.q: How does the rule of thirds divide the picture frame?
options: Into a grid of nine equal parts with two horizontal and two vertical lines
Into a central circle and outer ring
questions.explain: The rule of thirds splits the frame into a 3x3 grid, and placing subjects along the lines or intersections creates balanced compositions.

questions.q: You want to photograph a waterfall so the water appears as a smooth, silky blur. Which setting should you choose?
options: A narrow aperture such as f/22 alone
questions.explain: A slow shutter speed keeps the exposure open long enough to record the water's movement as a soft blur.

questions.q: To take a portrait where the subject is sharp but the background is softly blurred, which setting is most effective?
questions.explain: A wide aperture gives a shallow depth of field, isolating the subject against a blurred background.

questions.q: What are the three lights in a classic three-point lighting setup?
options: Key light, fill light and back light
Spot light, flood light and strobe
Hard light, soft light and side light
Top light, ground light and rim light
questions.explain: Three-point lighting uses a key light as the main source, a fill light to soften shadows, and a back light to separate the subject from the background.

questions.q: The term 'chiaroscuro' in photography refers to what?
options: Strong contrast between light and dark
A soft, even spread of light
A warm colour cast at sunset
questions.explain: Chiaroscuro, borrowed from painting, describes dramatic contrast between light and shadow used to create depth and mood.

questions.q: What is the 'golden hour' in photography?
options: The period shortly after sunrise or before sunset with warm, soft light
The middle of the day when the sun is highest
The hour after dark when artificial light is used
The time needed to develop a print
questions.explain: The golden hour occurs just after sunrise or before sunset, giving warm, soft, directional light favoured by photographers.

questions.q: Compared with hard light, what does soft light typically produce?
options: Soft, gradual shadows with gentle edges
Sharp, dark shadows with hard edges
questions.explain: Soft, diffused light wraps around a subject and produces gentle shadows with smooth transitions, flattering for portraits.

questions.q: The editing techniques 'dodging' and 'burning' originally come from what process?
options: Darkroom printing, to lighten or darken areas of a photograph
Framing with the rule of thirds
questions.explain: Dodging lightens and burning darkens selected areas; the terms come from traditional darkroom printing and are now replicated in editing software.

questions.q: How would you describe a high-key photograph?
options: Bright overall with low contrast and few dark shadows
Very dark with dominant shadows and small highlights
questions.explain: High-key lighting produces a bright, airy image with low contrast and minimal shadow, often used for clean, upbeat portraits.

questions.q: You want a moody portrait with deep shadows falling across one side of the face. Which lighting approach best achieves this?
options: Low-key lighting with a single, directional key light
High-key lighting with several soft fill lights
Flat, even lighting from the front
questions.explain: A single directional key light with little fill creates low-key lighting, casting deep shadows for a dramatic, moody effect.

questions.q: Henri Cartier-Bresson is most associated with which concept and genre?
options: The Zone System and landscape photography
questions.explain: Cartier-Bresson, a pioneer of street photography, coined the idea of the 'decisive moment' - capturing the instant when composition and action align.

questions.q: Ansel Adams is best known for which type of photography?
questions.explain: Ansel Adams is celebrated for his dramatic black and white landscapes of the American West and for developing the Zone System of tonal control.

questions.q: Cindy Sherman's photographic work is best described as what?
options: Staged self-portraiture exploring identity and roles
questions.explain: Cindy Sherman photographs herself in constructed characters and scenes, using staged self-portraiture to question identity and representation.

questions.q: Man Ray is known for creating cameraless images that he called what?
questions.explain: Man Ray made cameraless images by placing objects on light-sensitive paper and exposing them to light, which he named rayographs (a form of photogram).

questions.q: A student is producing a project on documentary photography that records social hardship. Whose work would be the most relevant reference?
questions.explain: Dorothea Lange is famed for documentary images of the Great Depression, such as 'Migrant Mother', making her ideal for a social documentary project.
